primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Sarcoidosis causes noncaseating granulomatous inflammation, commonly affecting hilar lymph nodes and lungs and sometimes skin, eyes, and calcium metabolism.
vignette: A 32-year-old woman has dry cough, dyspnea, erythema nodosum, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas.
distractor_notes: Tuberculosis typically produces caseating granulomas and infectious risk factors.
Histoplasmosis is an endemic fungal infection and usually requires compatible exposure evidence.
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis causes interstitial fibrosis and honeycombing rather than granulomas and hilar adenopathy.
COPD causes airflow obstruction and emphysema or chronic bronchitis.
key_expl: Bilateral hilar adenopathy with noncaseating granulomas and erythema nodosum strongly supports sarcoidosis.
objective: Recognize pulmonary sarcoidosis from characteristic imaging and pathology.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes sarcoidosis as granulomatous disease commonly affecting lungs and lymph nodes.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A one-way pleural air leak raises intrathoracic pressure, collapses the ipsilateral lung, shifts mediastinal structures, and obstructs venous return, causing shock.
vignette: A trauma patient develops severe dyspnea, hypotension, absent right breath sounds, distended neck veins, and tracheal deviation to the left.
lead: Which physiologic change most directly causes the hypotension?
correct: Reduced venous return from elevated intrathoracic pressure
distractor_notes: Contractility would not explain the obstructive shock pattern.
Histamine-mediated vasodilation causes distributive shock, not this unilateral thoracic emergency.
Oncotic pressure changes cause edema rather than acute obstructive hypotension.
Surfactant production is unrelated to the immediate hemodynamic collapse.
key_expl: Tension pneumothorax causes obstructive shock by compressing the great veins and reducing cardiac preload.
objective: Explain hypotension in tension pneumothorax through impaired venous return.

sources.title: Collapsed lung (pneumothorax)
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes tension pneumothorax as a life-threatening pressure buildup affecting breathing and circulation.

sources.title: Pneumothorax
sources.support: NHLBI describes pleural air accumulation and possible cardiovascular compromise.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Perfusion of poorly ventilated alveoli lowers local V/Q ratio and arterial oxygenation; supplemental oxygen usually improves hypoxemia unless a true shunt dominates.
vignette: A patient with lobar pneumonia has alveoli filled with inflammatory exudate but preserved blood flow through the affected region.
distractors: Pure diffusion limitation without V/Q change
distractor_notes: High V/Q occurs when ventilation exceeds perfusion, as in pulmonary embolic dead space.
An infinite V/Q ratio is dead-space ventilation with essentially no perfusion.
Consolidated but perfused alveoli are not normally matched.
Pneumonia directly reduces ventilation to perfused lung units.
key_expl: When ventilation falls while perfusion continues, the local V/Q ratio decreases.
objective: Identify low V/Q physiology in pneumonia.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes alveolar infection and filling that impairs gas exchange.

sources.title: Pneumonia
sources.support: NHLBI describes impaired oxygen exchange in pneumonia.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Pulmonary arterial obstruction creates ventilated alveoli with little or no perfusion, increasing physiologic dead space and regional V/Q toward infinity.
vignette: A pulmonary embolus abruptly blocks blood flow to a well-ventilated segment of lung.
lead: What happens to the local ventilation-perfusion ratio?
distractors: It equals mixed venous oxygen content
distractor_notes: A ratio near zero describes perfused but nonventilated shunt physiology.
V/Q of 1 indicates ideal matching, which is lost after perfusion is blocked.
V/Q ratios are not negative.
The ratio is independent of venous oxygen content.
key_expl: Ventilation with absent perfusion is alveolar dead space and drives V/Q toward infinity.
objective: Relate pulmonary embolism to high V/Q dead-space physiology.

sources.support: NHLBI describes pulmonary arterial obstruction and impaired perfusion in pulmonary embolism.

sources.title: Pulmonary embolism
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes sudden blockage of pulmonary blood flow.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Fluid accumulation in the pleural space compresses adjacent lung and produces decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion.
vignette: A patient with congestive heart failure develops progressive dyspnea. Examination shows decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at both lung bases.
distractor_notes: Pneumothorax causes hyperresonance rather than dullness.
Emphysema often causes diffuse hyperresonance and diminished breath sounds, not dependent dullness.
Asthma causes wheezing and airflow obstruction.
Pulmonary embolism often has a relatively normal lung examination.
key_expl: Dependent dullness to percussion with reduced breath sounds is classic pleural fluid accumulation.
objective: Recognize pleural effusion from physical examination findings.
clues: basilar dullness and reduced breath sounds

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes pleural fluid accumulation and associated respiratory findings.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Addition of unmeasured organic acids lowers serum bicarbonate and increases the anion gap.
vignette: A patient with diabetic ketoacidosis has sodium 138 mEq/L, chloride 102 mEq/L, and bicarbonate 10 mEq/L.
lead: What is the serum anion gap?
distractor_notes: 8 is the normal approximate lower range and is not the calculated value.
12 is a typical normal value but not the result here.
18 underestimates the unmeasured anions.
36 overestimates the calculation.
objective: Calculate the anion gap in metabolic acidosis.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes the anion gap as a calculated measure used to evaluate acid-base disorders.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes ketoacid accumulation causing metabolic acidosis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of gastric hydrochloric acid removes hydrogen and chloride while volume contraction increases renal bicarbonate retention and aldosterone activity.
vignette: A patient has several days of persistent vomiting and develops elevated serum bicarbonate and hypochloremia.
lead: Which primary acid-base disorder is most likely?
distractor_notes: Metabolic acidosis would lower bicarbonate.
Respiratory acidosis is caused by CO2 retention.
Respiratory alkalosis is caused by hyperventilation and low CO2.
The clinical history specifically causes hydrogen chloride loss and alkalosis.
key_expl: Loss of gastric acid from vomiting produces chloride-depletion metabolic alkalosis.
objective: Recognize vomiting as a cause of metabolic alkalosis.

sources.title: Metabolic alkalosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes vomiting and loss of gastric acid as causes of metabolic alkalosis.

sources.title: Electrolyte Panel
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes bicarbonate and chloride measurement in acid-base assessment.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Efferent arteriolar dilation lowers glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure and therefore lowers GFR, especially when renal perfusion is already reduced.
vignette: A patient with bilateral renal artery stenosis begins an ACE inhibitor and creatinine rises substantially.
lead: Which renal hemodynamic change most directly explains the fall in GFR?
distractors: Constriction of the afferent arteriole by angiotensin II
distractor_notes: Angiotensin II preferentially constricts the efferent arteriole; ACE inhibition reduces that effect.
GFR falls because glomerular pressure decreases, not increases.
A higher filtration coefficient would increase GFR.
Efferent constriction helps preserve glomerular pressure in low-perfusion states.
key_expl: ACE inhibition dilates the efferent arteriole, reducing intraglomerular pressure and GFR.
objective: Explain ACE-inhibitor-associated creatinine rise in renal artery stenosis.

sources.title: Renal artery stenosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes renal artery stenosis as reducing renal blood flow and causing renovascular hypertension.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Calcium oxalate supersaturation produces radiopaque stones with envelope- or dumbbell-shaped crystals; hypercalciuria is a common risk factor.
vignette: A 41-year-old man has sudden colicky flank pain radiating to the groin and microscopic hematuria. Urine shows envelope-shaped crystals.
lead: Which stone composition is most likely?
distractor_notes: Uric acid crystals are often rhomboid and stones are radiolucent.
Cystine crystals are hexagonal.
Struvite stones are associated with urease-positive infection and coffin-lid crystals.
Xanthine stones are rare and associated with purine metabolism disorders.
key_expl: Envelope-shaped crystals and classic renal colic most strongly indicate calcium oxalate stones.
objective: Recognize calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis from crystal morphology.

sources.support: MedlinePlus describes renal colic, hematuria, and common kidney stone types.

sources.title: Kidney Stones
sources.support: NIDDK describes calcium stones as the most common kidney stones.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Failure of alpha-intercalated cells to secrete hydrogen ions prevents urinary acidification, causing non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, high urine pH, hypokalemia, and nephrolithiasis.
vignette: A woman with autoimmune disease has non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, hypokalemia, urine pH 6.5, and recurrent calcium phosphate stones.
correct: Hydrogen ion secretion by alpha-intercalated cells
distractors: Bicarbonate reabsorption in proximal tubule only
Sodium chloride transport in thick ascending limb
distractor_notes: Proximal bicarbonate wasting causes type 2 RTA and urine can acidify once plasma bicarbonate falls.
Loop transport defects cause Bartter syndrome.
Aquaporin-2 defects cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
SGLT2 defects cause glucosuria.
key_expl: Distal RTA is failure to acidify urine through impaired distal hydrogen secretion.
objective: Differentiate distal RTA from proximal RTA using urine pH and nephrolithiasis.

sources.title: Renal tubular acidosis
sources.support: NIDDK describes distal RTA as impaired acid secretion causing metabolic acidosis and kidney stones.

sources.title: Renal tubular acidosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes kidney tubular acid-base defects.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Hypoaldosteronism or aldosterone resistance reduces distal sodium reabsorption and potassium/hydrogen secretion, causing hyperkalemic non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
vignette: A patient with diabetic kidney disease has mild non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and persistent hyperkalemia.
lead: Which hormonal abnormality most likely contributes?
distractors: Reduced cortisol only without mineralocorticoid effect
distractor_notes: Excess aldosterone causes hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis.
PTH affects calcium and phosphate.
Vasopressin controls water reabsorption.
Isolated cortisol deficiency does not directly produce the classic hyperkalemic RTA pattern unless mineralocorticoid function is also impaired.
key_expl: Type 4 RTA is the hyperkalemic RTA and usually reflects impaired aldosterone production or action.
objective: Recognize type 4 RTA from hyperkalemia and non-anion-gap acidosis.

sources.title: Renal tubular acidosis
sources.support: NIDDK describes type 4 RTA as related to low aldosterone or resistance and associated with high potassium.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: The thick ascending limb reabsorbs Na-K-2Cl while remaining water-impermeable, diluting tubular fluid and generating the corticomedullary osmotic gradient used for urine concentration.
vignette: A loop diuretic inhibits Na-K-2Cl transport in the thick ascending limb.
lead: Which renal concentrating mechanism is most directly impaired?
correct: Generation of the medullary osmotic gradient
distractor_notes: Glucose is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule.
Glomerular filtration is not the primary target of NKCC2 blockade.
The kidney does not produce urea in the collecting duct.
Renin is produced by juxtaglomerular cells, not hepatocytes.
key_expl: Salt reabsorption without water in the thick ascending limb drives countercurrent multiplication and medullary hypertonicity.
objective: Explain how the thick ascending limb supports urine concentration.

sources.title: Loop diuretics
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes loop diuretics as acting in the kidney to increase salt and water excretion.

sources.support: NIDDK describes nephron filtration and selective tubular reabsorption.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Urothelial carcinoma commonly presents with painless gross hematuria; cigarette smoking is a major risk factor due to urinary excretion of carcinogens.
vignette: A 66-year-old man with a 45-pack-year smoking history has several episodes of painless gross hematuria without dysuria.
distractor_notes: Cystitis usually causes dysuria, frequency, and urgency.
Nephrolithiasis usually causes severe colicky flank pain.
Glomerulonephritis often causes proteinuria and dysmorphic red cells or casts.
BPH causes obstructive urinary symptoms and can cause hematuria, but painless gross hematuria in a heavy smoker is a classic red flag for bladder cancer.
key_expl: Painless gross hematuria in an older smoker is classic for urothelial bladder cancer until proven otherwise.
objective: Recognize bladder cancer from painless hematuria and smoking risk.

sources.title: Bladder Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes hematuria and smoking as major features of bladder cancer.
